Commentary.Commentary: Into the new week, we go - Well, folks, that's all we have from Super Sunday, but the action in the 2026 ICC Men's T20 World Cup continues. On Monday, 23 February, the remaining two teams in Group 1 will go up against each other. It will be West Indies taking on Zimbabwe at the iconic Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai. That game will begin at 1.30 pm GMT, but as usual, you can join the build-up a lot sooner. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

Enjoy this win and then park it - The skipper of South Africa, Aiden Markram feels it was a different kind of wicket than they had previously. He applauds the way his boys adapted to the conditions and feels that the partnership between Dewald Brevis and David Miller steadied the ship. Reckons the wicket was spongy, so had to run hard in the second half of the innings. Admits that there wasn't the connectedness towards the game against the UAE, but feels they were all regrouped and connected for today's game, which made the difference. On Lungi Ngidi's performance, Aiden says he is a threat and can pick wickets in any conditions. He is a soldier and delivers for the team. Notes that the West Indies are playing really good cricket, and they are looking forward to that match.

Nothing changes after one loss - The Indian captain​​​​​​, Suryakumar Yadav believes that his side bowled well, but South Africa batted well between overs 7 and 15 and admits they could have batted better. Feels that you cannot win the game in the Powerplay, but you can lose it and losing too many wickets early meant they could not build the partnerships they needed. He acknowledges the impact of the Arshdeep and Bumrah combination, saying everyone knows what they bring to the side. Tells that nothing changes because of one loss, and he wants his team to continue playing the brand of cricket they have been playing till now.
Let's now hear what the two captains have to say...

Player of the Match - World Test Championship-winning captain, Temba Bavuma, hands the award to David Miller for his game-changing knock of 63 runs in just 35 balls. He says they were behind the eight ball when they were 20/3 and didn't want to go in the shell, so it was nice to hit a couple of boundaries along with Dewald Brevis. Reckons that this wicket demanded to hit more straight than square. It wasn't spinning too much, so they tried to take on the spinners. Shares that India have some world-class bowlers and they just tried to match the intensity.

The hosts get a taste of their own medicine - India have been, without a doubt, the best T20 outfit in the international game over the last couple of years but they have been humbled by the Proteas, who came in with a plan and executed things perfectly. India have been vulnerable with the bat during the course of the tournament but given it is such a deep batting lineup and the bowling has been so good, that they have gotten away with it, not today, though. India got the perfect start with the ball as Jasprit Bumrah once again showed why he is the most feared bowler in the world. However, the spinners failed to make an impact and Varun Chakaravarthy had a rare shoddy outing. Bumrah and co did pull things back a bit at the death but Hardik Pandya went for 20 runs in the final over and the momentum swayed South Africa's way. With the bat, the less we speak, the better. As many as 8 top-class T20 batters and yet India only managed to get 111 runs. Once again, the opening stand didn't work out and this time, it was Ishan Kishan who got out for a duck. Abhishek Sharma huffed and puffed his way to 15 runs and Suryakumar Yadav also got a start but barring Shivam Dube, no one made any sort of an impact and things went out of reach too soon.

Proteas take revenge and then some - South Africa will have that evening in Barbados from a couple of years ago in the back of their mind heading into this clash. And boy, they have completely flipped the script on its head and have dealt a big blow to the host nation, India, who are dubbed as the favorites to win the competition. They stuttered with the bat early on, losing 3 wickets for just 20 runs but then came their crisis-man, David Miller and along with Dewald Brevis, shifted the momentum of the first innings. Their stand, worth 97 runs, was the highlight of the Proteas batting innings. Tristan Stubbs' late burst in the final over took them to a solid total of 187 runs. With the ball, South Africa returned fire and had India in all sorts of bother inside the Powerplay. Aiden Markram's decision to open the bowling against the two left-handed openers worked like a charm as he got rid of an in-form Ishan Kishan. The pacers then followed up and kept pressing. The catching was fantastic, and the changes in pace and in lengths were just spot-on from the Proteas. Marco Jansen was the standout with his four-fer as the likes of Keshav Maharaj and Corbin Bosch picked up five wickets between them.

A double bashing of the hosts - Sri Lanka earlier in the day and India now, the first Super Sunday of the Super Eight stage has seen the two co-hosts being handed hefty defeats, and in the process, both of them have been derailed off the tracks right now. The Proteas, on the other hand, have made Ahmedabad a second home and have outplayed the reigning champions, handing them a first defeat in Men's T20 World Cup matches after 12 straight wins.

OUT! TAKEN! A thumping win for South Africa by 76 runs. Pace taken off, full and pushed across the right-hander, Bumrah extends his hands into the lofted drive. Gets it right off the toe end of the blade, and it is spooned to extra cover, where Aiden Markram circles under it on the edge of the ring and makes no mistake. Two in two for Jansen to complete a statement win for the Proteas.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Keshav Maharaj to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Skidding through, not all that short, on middle. Sundar presses on the back foot and pulls it through mid-wicket for one more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Keshav Maharaj to Washington Sundar, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a nagging length, around off, Suryakumar gets down on a knee and plays the sweep to deep backward square leg. Kagiso Rabada reads the spin on the ball and tidies up. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Keshav Maharaj to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! Two ordinary Powerplays with the bat from the two batting sides. South Africa managed 41/3 but India are 10 runs worse at 31/3 at the same stage. The game did change in the middle phase and India will be hoping that the ball slides on a bit better now. The Proteas have been very smart with their off-pace deliveries and will look to use those variations throughout the innings. With that said, Keshav Maharaj comes on to bowl right after the fielding restrictions are lifted.
Rabada goes searching for the yorker but it comes out as a low full toss, on middle. SKY punches it straight to mid on. Just 2 runs off the over, India end their Powerplay at 31/3.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Kagiso Rabada to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angled away, on a short of a length, Sundar stands tall to get this one over the in-field on the off side. Gets it off the outer half to deep third, where Dewald Brevis slides and mops it up. Just a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Kagiso Rabada to Washington Sundar, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Make that four on the bounce! Pushes the length up, on middle. Sundar clears the front leg and knocks it along the ground to mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Kagiso Rabada to Washington Sundar, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Rabada serves a short ball, on off. Washington Sundar arches back to play the upper cut but he is beaten for pace. Three dots in a row!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Kagiso Rabada to Washington Sundar, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On the fuller side, pushed across off, Washington walks across the stumps to play the scoop but plays all over it. Gets rapped on the pads well outside the off stump.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Kagiso Rabada to Washington Sundar, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Rabada hits the hard length, on top of off. Sundar plays it on the up but mistimes it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Kagiso Rabada to Washington Sundar, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angled into the pads, this is turned to deep square leg for a single. End of a successful over for Jansen and South Africa.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Marco Jansen to Washington Sundar, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and on middle, Suryakumar Yadav pushes it to the right of mid off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Marco Jansen to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Around off, on a good length, Sundar dabs it wide of point and takes a single to get underway.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Marco Jansen to Washington Sundar, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: The next batter is Washington Sundar, in at number 5.

OUT! CAUGHT! Two fielders bump into each other, but Corbin Bosch holds onto it. A massive wicket for South Africa. This is the knuckleball from Jansen, full and on middle. Abhishek does not pick the variation. He clears the front leg and has a swipe across the line. Skies it off the toe end of the blade over wide mid on. Corbin Bosch and Keshav Maharaj go after it from mid-wicket and mid on, respectively, and there is no communication between the two men. Maharaj just about withdraws himself but cannot avoid colliding with Bosch. Corbin stretches his hands out in front and the ball hits him near the wrist but he holds onto it near his chest. Keshav falls on the back of Bosch but the latter is not put off by that and he grabs hold of the ball.
Commentary.Howout: c Corbin Bosch b Marco Jansen
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, OUT! c Corbin Bosch b Marco Jansen.

Commentary.Commentary: Has that been taken? My word, that could have ended up being a nasty collision between Keshav Maharaj and Corbin Bosch but the latter seems to have taken a stunning catch. It is quickly confirmed to be a fair catch and that's the end of Abhishek Sharma.
In the channel, on a back of a length. Abhishek dances down the track and backs away. He throws the kitchen sink at it but fails to connect.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bashes the surface, over middle. Sharma hops and swivels to help it over long leg but he is hurried and the ball gets big on him. Abhishek wears it on the midriff.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Marco Jansen switches ends now, replacing Kagiso Rabada. He went for 8 runs in his first over and picked up a wicket as well.
Yes, he can! Drops it full and on middle, slower and dipping right onto the batter. Sharma plays with soft hands to cover and runs across.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Lungi Ngidi to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Excellent so far from Ngidi! Keeps it full and across the batter, too wide and again on the slower side. Abhishek reaches as he bends across and plays it to cover. Can he close it out well?
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Lungi Ngidi to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Oh, a bit harsh on the bowler! Lungi Ngidi stays away from the hitting arc and bowls the off-cutter near the tramline. Sharma tries to dig it away but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Lungi Ngidi to Abhishek Sharma, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Overpitches it outside off. Yadav stays back and wrists it away to mid on. Kagiso Rabada puts in a full-stretched dive to his left to stop it from running away. Just a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Lungi Ngidi to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Three dots to start for Ngidi! Pace-off once again, fuller and just outside off. Suryakumar Yadav punches it to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Lungi Ngidi to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Well bowled! Ngidi bowls the off-cutter, fuller and well outside off. Yadav shapes for the paddle-scoop but ends up patting it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Lungi Ngidi to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Lungi Ngidi starts with a length delivery, attacking the stumps, holds a bit into the surface. Yadav taps it into the strip.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Lungi Ngidi to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Crunched away! Kagiso Rabada rolls his fingers but dishes out a full toss, outside off. Sharma uses the width and hammers it past cover-point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Kagiso Rabada to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: On a good length and around leg, tight from KG, following Sharma on the leg side. Abhishek ends up dropping it to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Kagiso Rabada to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Smartly played by Sharma and this will give him confidence. Sharma waits for the ball to arrive, sees the short ball and ramps it nicely over the keeper and all the way for six runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Kagiso Rabada to Abhishek Sharma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Another dot! Sharma is throwing his hands on everything. Rabada keeps it fuller and around the sixth stump line. Sharma flashes his blade and misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Kagiso Rabada to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten again! Rabada sees Sharma take the charge and digs into the surface, around off. Abhishek backs away and opens up the off side but fails to hit it away. The ball flies over the off pole.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Kagiso Rabada to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! KG pitches it up, just outside off. Abhishek Sharma throws his blade but the ball just nips away enough to beat the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Kagiso Rabada to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Will Markram give himself another over? Nope, just one quick productive over for the skipper. In comes Kagiso Rabada.
8 runs and a wicket off the over. Jansen bowls on a nagging length, around off and slanting away. SKY knocks it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Marco Jansen to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good shot for no run. Jansen offers width once again, well outside off. Suryakumar Yadav crisply hits it away but straight to the extra-cover fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Marco Jansen to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Superb timing once again! Back of a length, outside off, angling across the batter. Suryakumar Yadav gets tall and punches it firmly past cover for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Marco Jansen to Suryakumar Yadav, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Jansen keeps it full and on middle and leg. Yadav flicks it nicely but straight to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Marco Jansen to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Wrist work from the skipper to get his inning underway! A straighter, fuller delivery on the pads. Suryakumar Yadav gets the bottom hand into play as he flicks it past mid-wicket for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Marco Jansen to Suryakumar Yadav, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: India are 5/2. Remember, South Africa were 20/3 as well early on. With that said, the Indian skipper, Suryakumar Yadav walks out to bat now.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! South Africa celebrates as Varma nicks one behind, but he is not sure. Varma takes it upstairs. There was a sound as the ball passed the blade. UltraEdge loads and shows a big spike. Not sure why Tilak Varma reviewed that one. Marco Jansen steams in and serves it into the surface, touch fuller and gets it to bounce off the deck, outside off. Tilak Varma charges down the track and tries to push away from his body and edges it to the keeper. Quinton de Kock pouches it safely.
Commentary.Howout: c Quinton de Kock b Marco Jansen
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Marco Jansen to Tilak Varma, OUT! c Quinton de Kock b Marco Jansen.

Commentary.Commentary: It will be Marco Jansen with his left-arm medium pacers, to bowl from the other end.

FOUR! After three outings, Abhishek Sharma is finally off the mark in the tournament. Huge sigh of relief for India's dynamic opener. Markram drops it short and offers room outside off. Sharma slashes his blade and finds the gap through cover-point and bags a boundary. 5 runs and a wicket off the first over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Aiden Markram to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: India and Tilak Varma are underway. This is full and around off, Varma knocks it down to long off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Aiden Markram to Tilak Varma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A masterstroke from Aiden Markram and he gets the in-form batter out in the very first over. Tilak Varma walks in at number 3.

OUT! TAKEN! It's Kishan who departs on a duck this time! Indian openers are yet to give a breakthrough opening stand this tournament. Nicely tossed up, around off, turning slightly away. Kishan gets on his knee to slog but gets a top edge. Pretty high in the air but not far away. Ryan Rickelton, inside the ring, tracks back at cover and holds onto the skier.
Commentary.Howout: c Ryan Rickelton b Aiden Markram
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Aiden Markram to Ishan Kishan, OUT! c Ryan Rickelton b Aiden Markram.

Commentary.Commentary: Dew on the ground? Robin Uthappa on air certainly feels so.

JUST SHORT! Markram dips a fuller delivery onto the batter, this is on middle. Kishan bends and gets underneath as he tries to take on mid on but fails to get the elevation. Luckily for him, it falls short of the fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Aiden Markram to Ishan Kishan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tosses it up, fuller and around off. Ishan Kishan leans and taps it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Aiden Markram to Ishan Kishan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slightly short from Markram up front, outside off. Kishan flashes his blade ferociously but finds the point fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Aiden Markram to Ishan Kishan, No run.
